FOREWORD

This Indian Standard (SecondRevision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Foodgralns,Foodgrain Industriesand StarchesSectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Various terms connoting the same foodgrains or for denoting their quality are being used in the foodgrain trade in India at present. In order to (acilitate transactions on the basis of a uniform terminology coveringauthoritauve definitions of these terms. the Sectional Committee decided to formulate this standard.
This standard was first publishedin 1964 and SUbsequently revised in 1970. It is revised again to include

definitions for weeviled and dehuskedgrainsaswell to alignwiththe ISO5526 : 1986 'Cereals,pulses and other foodgrains - Nomenclature'.

3.6.7 Slightly Damaged or Touched Kernels or pieces of kernels that are damaged or discoloured, superficially so as not to affect the quality of the material.

Kernels or piecesof kernelshaving more than onefourth of the surfacecovered with red cuticle.

Kernelsor piecesof kernels that havechanged the colour as a result of deteriorative changes.

Pieces of kernels that are less than one-eighth of the size of the full kernels.

Kernelsthat are partiallyor wholly bored by insects injurious to grain.

Extent to which bran exclusive of germ portion is removed.

Review or Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards arc also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reamrme4~~hen such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changesare needed. it is taken up Cor revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by . referring to the latest issue of '8IS Handbook' and 'Standards Monthly Additions'.
